correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact standard-incidence six-class equations, their parameter restrictions and the threshold in the motivating source. For each real fractional order, the scalar Caputo resolvent has nonnegative, integrable forcing kernel and nonintegrable homogeneous Mittag-Leffler tail. The subcritical positive three-class comparison matrix has spectral radius sqrt(R0)<1; a strict constant supersolution and vector limsup contraction yield global decay. Stable scalar filters show T,R->0 and S->b/d. Each seeded infected class has a nonintegrable homogeneous lower bound, and Tonelli plus positive transfer rates propagate divergence to E,I,A,new infection and T. A separate exponentially stable classical-order comparison proves finiteness at order one. SymPy exact matrix/parameter checks were run on the packaged checker; finite checks are not substituted for infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: A direct source- and implication-level comparison shows that the motivating six-compartment unequal-order paper supplies local rational-order stability and finite-horizon burden only. The closest same-network 2026 article gives global disease-free stability for one common Caputo order but not the mixed-order comparison or infinite ordinary-time integrals. The 2025/2026 incommensurate SI literature proves local/global thresholds for two-class spatial models without the six-class treatment cascade. The scalar Mittag-Leffler tail theorem is known; its propagation through the full nonlinear infected-treatment graph to force simultaneous global clearance and divergence of all five natural burdens is not stated by these papers. Targeted source-title, claim and formula searches returned no equivalent or stronger published assertion.
residual_risks: A non-indexed preprint, erratum, or general published theorem specialized to the same six-compartment multi-order network could entail the conjunction; indexing noncoverage alone does not rule this out.
The 1948 original paper was not newly inspected in full; the standard theorem is identifiable by DOI and corroborated by modern open access literature.
The physical meaning of all-time ordinary-time integrals of effective fractional-order-rate model variables is limited and should not be reported as actual cumulative cases or treatment admissions.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A main applied output in both source articles is the time-integrated treatment or active infection burden. The theorem reveals a sharp and operationally relevant distinction: strict threshold-driven instantaneous eradication does not make an unweighted infinite-horizon burden finite in the stated fractional equations, and in fact no seeded transmission pathway escapes this defect. The all-class result is not the scalar Mittag-Leffler tail restated: it requires a nonlinear standard-incidence domination and graph-wide propagation between distinct orders, with a meaningful treatment parameter boundary and classical-order contrast. It limits how finite-horizon burdens may be mathematically extrapolated while explicitly restricting any empirical interpretation.
